Northwind Semiconductor beats on revenue, guides above consensus

Posted 23 October 2026 by R. Okafor

Northwind Semiconductor reported third-quarter revenue of $4.12 billion after the bell on Thursday, up 31% from a year earlier and ahead of the $3.95 billion analysts had expected.
Adjusted earnings per share came in at $1.87, against estimates of $1.71.

The company guided fourth-quarter revenue to between $4.35 billion and $4.55 billion. The midpoint, $4.45 billion, is about 6% above the consensus forecast of $4.20 billion.

Key numbers from the release:

  • Data-center revenue: $2.61 billion, up 58% year on year.
  • Gross margin: 61.4%, up from 57.9%.
  • Share buyback: a new $5 billion authorisation.

Chief executive Lena Varga said demand for the company's networking chips "continues to outrun supply" and that a second fabrication partner would begin shipping in the first quarter of 2027.

The stock rose 8.2% to $212.40 in extended trading. It had fallen 4% over the previous month on worries about a slowdown in cloud spending.

Analysts at two brokers raised their price targets after the call, citing the margin improvement. One noted that inventory fell for a third straight quarter, to 112 days of supply.

Not everything was rosy: the client PC segment grew only 6%, and management declined to give a 2027 outlook, saying it would do so at an investor day in February.
